exposure: Dystocic labor (before 4 hours of full cervical dilatation)
Dystocic labor (after 4 hours of full cervical dilatation)
cohort: Participants were pregnant women from whom lower uterine segment (LUS) fragments were collected during cesarean section.
finding: In dystocic labor lasting more than 4 hours from complete cervical ripening and dilatation, the concentration of laminin and collagen IV reduces in the LUS tissue, leading to decreased elasticity, increased roughness, and dryness of connective tissues.
cross-section timing: Tissue fragments were collected during cesarean section, comparing samples based on labor characteristics at that time.
